correctness.rationale: The GL-orbit classification of tuples by row space is exact; one-point extensions are precisely the functional graph row spaces and, when the ambient dimension permits, the independent cylinder. The resulting exact Hintikka recursion covers every formula of bounded rank. Finite exhaustive recurrence computes all root types through rank seven up to dimension eight, with a separate direct-element checker for base cases. For all dimensions at least q, a q-round game sees no span of rank q and the full independent extension is universally available; thus the finite computed plateau from dimension five is valid at every larger dimension. The distinct low-dimensional root types prove sharpness.

value.rationale: In the ternary relational language, finite binary vector-space elementary equivalence is a nontrivial bounded-quantifier-resource invariant since arbitrary long linear terms are not atomic. The complete seven-rank dimension partition reveals plateaux at ranks four and seven, an exact dimension-five visibility threshold, and a sharp finite representative bound of 32; these structural phenomena are motivated by distinguishing complexity and not a routine reinterpretation of the ambient vector dimension.
